knowledge_units.context_summary: The study presents the first direct experimental visualization of π-holes in molecules using Kelvin probe force microscopy. It explains how substituting peripheral hydrogens in polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons with more electronegative atoms creates electron-deficient cavities that alter electrostatic interactions.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text explains how electrostatic interactions, specifically quadrupole-quadrupole forces, stabilize heterodimers of benzene and hexafluorobenzene, highlighting the role of pi-holes. It notes that while pi-holes were previously only theoretically predicted or indirectly observed, Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) allows for direct visualization. The study experimentally confirms the presence of a pi-hole in 9,10-Dichlorooctafluoroanthracene (FCl-An) and its absence in anthracene (An) using KPFM and nc-AFM on a gold surface.

knowledge_units.context_summary: High-resolution nc-AFM and DFT calculations resolved the supramolecular assembly of anthracene and 9,10-dichlorooctafluoroanthracene on Au(111), revealing a rhombic structure driven by electrostatic interactions. While nc-AFM images showed similar contrast for both molecules, Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) was employed to map charge distributions with atomic resolution. The study notes that KPFM contrast is highly dependent on tip-sample distance, with submolecular features emerging at shorter distances but risking artifacts from tip relaxation.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study uses Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to visualize the π-hole in 9,10-dichlorooctafluoroanthracene (FCl-An) and compares its adsorption properties with anthracene (An) on Au(111). KPFM simulations using the PP-AFM code reproduce the experimental bow-tie pattern of the local contact potential difference (LCPD), which corresponds to the electrostatic potential distribution. Force-distance spectroscopy reveals that FCl-An adsorbs at a greater height (360 pm) than An (330 pm) due to suppressed charge induction caused by the π-hole.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study explains that the π-hole in FCl-An increases ionization potential, suppressing charge induction at the metal interface compared to An. SAPT0 analysis confirms that dispersion energy dominates the adsorption interaction for both molecules, while induction energy is higher for An. Experimental methods involved KPFM and nc-AFM imaging at 4.2 K on Au(111) substrates.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The study details the computational protocols for geometry optimization, AFM/KPFM simulation, and SAPT0 analysis of anthracene and FCl-An molecules on Au(111). Specific parameters for DFT functionals, basis sets, and force constraints were defined to model molecular-surface interactions. The simulations utilized a Probe Particle model with a CO-terminated tip to replicate experimental imaging conditions.

attributes.relaxation_constraint: molecule fully relaxed, gold layer atoms fixed
